record.original_question: Given n points in space with no four coplanar, determine the largest integer m for which one can guarantee that some m of the n points are the vertices of a convex polyhedron.

evidence.quote: Given n points in space, four by four non-coplanar, find a maximum m having the property that there are m points among n ones that constitute the vertexes of a convex polyhedron.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 4$ be a positive integer, and consider configurations of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ in general position in the sense that no four of the points are coplanar. A set of points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is said to form the vertices of a convex polyhedron if the points are the extreme points (vertices) of their convex hull, i.e., each point lies on the boundary of the convex hull and is not a convex combination of the others.

Determine the largest integer $m = m(n)$ such that every configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with no four coplanar contains some subset of $m$ points that form the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Equivalently, find the exact growth rate of $m(n)$, and for each $n$ determine the minimum number $N_3(m)$ of points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that guarantees the existence of $m$ points in convex position.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the 3-dimensional analogue of the Erdős–Szekeres "happy ending" problem. Only small exact values are known (e.g., $N_3(6)=9$, due to Bisztriczky and Soltan), and the exact value/growth rate of the function in general remains open. A conjectured recurrence $N_d(n)=4N_{d-1}(n-d)-3$ exists but is unproven; recent advances by Suk and others address the 2D case, while the higher-dimensional version remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Erdős-Szekeres problem on points in convex position - a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Grünbaum's higher-dimensional variant: existence of minimum N_d(n) such that any N_d(n) points in general position in E^d contain n points in convex position; exact values largely unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The higher-dimensional Erdős–Szekeres problem, including the 3D case for general m, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Happy ending problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations to higher dimensions and to convex position problems remain open beyond small cases.
status_evidence.claim: Exact values of the function are known only in small cases.

status_evidence.title: On the Erdős–Szekeres convex polygon problem (Suk)
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves asymptotic of the 2D Erdős–Szekeres function; higher-dimensional analogues not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Even after Suk's resolution of the planar asymptotics, the 3D analogue remains open.
